title: Eli Wilner December Frame Funding Program
summary: Eli Wilner & Company has announced that all funding allocated through its museum grant program for November 2026 has been fully committed in support of reframing and frame restoration projects at museums and cultural institutions nationwide. In response to continued demand, Eli Wilner & Company funding partners have committed an additional $150,000 for the December 2026 funding cycle, available exclusively to not-for-profit institutions. These funds will be awarded on a first-come, first-served basis through December 31, 2026, or until fully committed. The grants are intended to offset 50% of the cost of qualifying frame restoration and reframing projects to be completed by the Eli Wilner & Company studio. Recipient institutions are required to cover the remaining 50% of the approved project cost. title: New research argues Leonardo da Vinci left works unfinished as a deliberate protest against power
summary: Leonardo da Vinci was not only a genius. He was an observer of men. He studied them, deciphered them, anticipated them. Above all when they were powerful. And his most sophisticated tool, according to the new research presented in Florence, was not the brush. It was not finishing. This thesis was at the heart of the international conference «La Bellezza Ideale – La rinascita dell'Accademia Neoplatonica» (Ideal Beauty – The Rebirth of the Neoplatonic Academy), held on November 7 in the Sala del Pegaso of Palazzo Strozzi Sacrati, on the occasion of the world premiere presentation of the complete facsimile of the Madrid Codices I and II, produced by cARTEm, together with the volume Leonardo Svelato (Leonardo Unveiled) by Annalisa Di Maria and the scientific insights of Andrea

title: Robert Mapplethorpe show at Mai 36 Galerie pairs iconic works from 1979 to 1988
summary: Mai 36 Galerie is presenting Double Take, its seventh exhibition devoted to the American photographer Robert Mapplethorpe (1946-1989). Bringing together works from 1979 to 1988, the exhibition explores the artist’s fascination with dualities, pairing images to create dialogue, depth and friction. The preoccupation with dualities and the blurring of binaries was a fundamental aspect of his artistic practice that defined him throughout his career. Mapplethorpe lived between opposing worlds. His strict Catholic upbringing stood in stark contrast to his deep immersion in the radical counterculture of 1970s and 1980s New York, and his visual language grew from the friction between the two: weaponized symmetry, dramatic lighting, and thematic juxtaposition. Yet he never saw these opposites as mutually exclusive. Within the classical frame, what seemed contradictory could exist in perfect harmony, for, as he put it, “beauty and the devil are the same thing.” Throughout his prol

title: Rare Medieval and Renaissance treasures from London's V&A set for exclusive AGSA exhibition
summary: The Art Gallery of South Australia has today announced its artistic program for 2027, including the second Winter Art Series exhibition Medieval and Renaissance Treasures from the V&A, an exclusive showcase of extraordinary Medieval and Renaissance masterworks from the Victoria and Albert Museum, London. Other highlights across the year include a major survey of renowned South Australian fashion couturier Paolo Sebastian, a landmark presentation of Yolŋu women’s art and culture, Yunupiŋu: Seven Sisters as part of the 2027 Tarnanthi Festival, and an exhibition of rarely seen woodblock prints from Japan’s historic Kamigata region. title: The most sought-after Rolex of all: A 1967 Rolex Daytona 'Paul Newman' to be offered at auction in Paris
summary: Osenat’s Watches sale in Paris on 16 December 2026 will be led by one of the most sought-after watches a Rolex collector can hope to find: an exceptional 1967 Cosmograph Daytona reference 6241, the celebrated ‘Paul Newman’. Few watches carry quite the same mystique. The model owes its name to Paul Newman, the Hollywood star and keen amateur racing driver, who was rarely seen without a Daytona bearing this distinctive dial. His own watch, a gift from his wife Joanne Woodward, passed into legend when it sold for $17.8 million in 2017. That result confirmed the ‘Paul Newman’ as one of the most iconic and coveted watches in the world. Made in the 1960s, the reference 6241 is among the earliest black-bezel Daytonas. Its ‘exotic’ dials, with contrasting sub-dials and distinctive lettering, are now some of the most prized in vintage Rolex. title: Ben Brown Fine Arts examines the Düsseldorf School's photographic revolution in new exhibition
summary: Ben Brown Fine Arts is presenting The Architecture of Seeing: Photography and the Düsseldorf School, an exhibition of photography originating from the Kunstakademie Düsseldorf after 1976. Alongside Bernd and Hilla Becher, the exhibition brings together their students Andreas Gursky, Candida Höfer, Thomas Ruff and Thomas Struth, whose varying interpretations of the German ‘New Objectivity’ style championed by the Bechers revolutionised the photographic medium and opened up new ways of seeing. When Bernd Becher was appointed to the academy’s first professorship of photography in 1976, he and Hilla brought with them a method built on seriality, formal restraint and objective observation, sharpened by its dialogue with Minimal and Conceptual art. title: Christie's Hong Kong Handbags & Accessories sale totals HK$59.5M, setting annual Asia record
summary: On 23 November 2026, Christie's Handbags & Accessories sale, held during Hong Kong Luxury Week, achieved a total of HK$59,534,080 / US$7,591,250. The result brought the category's annual sales total to HK$172,896,060 / US$22,046,149, the highest annual Asia sales total in the category to date, leading the global auction market for Handbags & Accessories. The sale was 93% sold by lot, with a hammer total 126% above the low estimate. Strong global participation was seen from collectors across 31 countries and five continents, led by Greater China and followed by Southeast Asia. Bidding was particularly active online, with 67% of lots sold through Christie's digital platforms. New buyers represented 25% of participants in the sale, with Millennials and Gen Z accounting for nearly 60% of this group, reflecting the category's enduring appeal among both new and seasoned collectors. title: Missing for decades, Rimtas Kalpokas's 1939 World's Fair painting found beside a dumpster in Vilnius
summary: On Tuesday, 24 November, the Pranas Gudynas Conservation Centre of the Lithuanian National Museum of Art (LNMA) presented the canvas titled The Coronation of the First King of Lithuania Mindaugas in 1253 by Rimtas Kalpokas, an artwork that has been missing for decades. The artist created the painting in 1939 for the Lithuanian Pavilion at the New York World’s Fair. The canvas, discarded near a trash container in the Vilnius neighborhood of Žvėrynas was spotted by Danutė and Jonas Juozelskai, who notified the Pranas Gudynas Conservation Centre about their find. Upon arriving to inspect at the artwork, conservation project coordinator Rasa Misevičienė and conservator of easel painting Lina Jurnienė recognized it as the historic canvas by Rimtas Kalpokas. title: Sole highest-graded Conan first appearance leads stellar Heritage Pulp Magazines Auction
summary: Pulp magazine collectors can spend a lifetime chasing the hobby’s grail of grails, its Action Comics No. 1 or T206 Honus Wagner card: The All-Story No. 94 from October 1912, boasting the first appearance of Edgar Rice Burroughs’ massively popular Tarzan. At Heritage’s Dec. 4–5 Pulp Magazines Signature® Auction, the most serious collectors in the hobby have two opportunities to capture this most elusive of prey. The auction is the follow-up to June’s $1.8 million-plus Pulp Magazines Signature® Auction, which set numerous price records including the highest total results for a pulps auction. That event was led by a CGC 2.0 copy of the UK Price Variant The All-Story No. 94. This time around, bidders will battle for the second-highest-graded unrestored copy on the census, a CGC 2.5 copy of the title that introduced the King of the Jungle to the world. title: Caroline Shields named Robert and Martha Berman Lipp Chief Curator of Clark Art Institute
summary: The Clark Art Institute appointed Caroline Shields to be the new Robert and Martha Berman Lipp Chief Curator effective January, 2027. The announcement followed an international search for an accomplished scholar and curator to oversee the curatorial department of one of the nation's most distinguished collections of European and American art encompassing paintings, sculpture, works on paper, and decorative arts. “In Caroline Shields, we have found an excellent leader and a talented manager of curatorial projects. Caroline is well known to us for her exhibitions and scholarship, and we are confident she will expertly steward our ever-evolving collection,” said Esther Bell, Hardymon Director of the Clark. title: Gooding Christie's inaugural Retromobile New York sale achieves over $51 million
summary: Gooding Christie's reports over $51 million in total sales from its inaugural sale at the Javits Center, which took place on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21. A total of 146 lots sold throughout the two days of auction, culminating in a strong 92% sell-through rate. The top lot of the sale was the 1967 Ferrari 275 GTB/4*S NART Spider first owned by legendary actor Steve McQueen, which sold for $18,925,000. The entirety of the Billy Joel Motorcycle Collection sold on Saturday, generating more than $2 million in sales and surpassing its combined pre-auction estimate by a factor of four. In addition to the NART Spider, a number of blue-chip European classics garnered strong results on Friday, including the 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Alloy Gullwing, which sold for $4,735,000. title: Nature's artistry takes center stage in Heritage's Fine Mineral Premier Selection Auction Dec. 5
summary: A stunning Fluorite from Minerva’s No. 1 Mine in Illinois, with multiple vibrant colors showing through a remarkably glassy surface, will shimmer in the spotlight when it is offered in Heritage’s Dec. 5 Fine Mineral Premier Selection Signature® Auction. “When curating this auction,” says Nic Valenzuela, Heritage Auctions’ Director of Fine Minerals, “we focused on specimens that showed exceptional crystallization, or some form of significance to a given species while commanding excellent aesthetics.” The Fluorite from the Minerva No. 1 Mine, Illinois, is a magnificent example from a mine that produces specimens coveted by serious collectors. Measuring 2.91 inches (7.4 cm) in height, it boasts a marvelous assemblage of beautifully formed and extremely colorful Fluorite cubes, the largest of which rises above the very peak of the specimen and measures a respectable 4.5 centimeters in size. title: Kunsthalle Wien presents major Magali Reus survey featuring over 80 sculptures
summary: Kunsthalle Wien presents a solo exhibition by Magali Reus (b. 1981, The Hague). Tenant brings together over 80 sculptural works produced between 2014 and 2026. Installed within a specially-conceived architecture that occupies the first floor of Kunsthalle Wien’s Museumsquartier building, it is one of the largest exhibitions of Reus’ work to date and the first in Austria. The work of Magali Reus is rooted in keen observation of the vernacular, the wildly absurd details of everyday life. Vessels such as jam jars, sardine tins, washing detergent packaging and pizza boxes are the subjects of sculptural investigations in which forms are translated, altered and remade in series. Scaled-up and combined with other imagery, Reus defamiliarises these objects, changing their orientation, colours, materials and surfaces. title: Talbot Rice Gallery unveils 2027 programme with Dana Awartani and Fiona Lutjenhuis solos
summary: Talbot Rice Gallery announced the 2027 exhibitions programme, featuring a major solo exhibition of Dana Awartani, a group exhibition The Isles of Many Gods, the continuation of the group exhibition The Rupture: No condition is permanent, the first solo exhibition of Fiona Lutjenhuis in the UK, and the biennial student exhibition—Trading Zone 2027. The Rupture is an international collaboration between Talbot Rice Gallery, University of Edinburgh; Inside-Out Art Museum, Beijing; and the Museum of Contemporary Art and Design, Manila. The three-part project responds to profound global changes in political, social, economic and security conditions, and at Talbot Rice Gallery includes Taysir Batniji, Jenny Brady, Dasha Chechushkova, Jasmina Cibic, Kiri Dalena, Zhanna Kadyrova, Roman Khimei and Yarema Malashchuk, Tarik Kiswanson,

title: Gladstone adds Scottish painter Andrew Cranston to its roster alongside Modern Art and Ingleby Gallery
summary: Gladstone announces representation of Scottish artist Andrew Cranston in collaboration with Modern Art, London and Ingleby Gallery, Edinburgh. Known for his distinctive approach to painting, Cranston draws from an expansive repertoire of visual and literary sources, moving fluidly between art-historical reference, personal anecdote and the peculiarities of everyday experience. His paintings occupy an ambiguous territory between observation and invention, where familiar subjects give way to unexpected narratives and associations. Cranston engages with painting as an open-ended process, allowing images to evolve through successive acts of addition, revision, and concealment. title: $96,875 for 'Super Mario Bros.' sets complete-in-box game world record at $2.5 million Heritage Video Games Auction
summary: A PSA 9.0 complete-in-box copy of the 1985 matte-sticker first-production run variant of Super Mario Bros. jumped to $96,875 to set two world records at Heritage Auctions’ $2,516,830 Nov. 20–21 Video Games Signature® Auction: highest price for a first-production copy of Super Mario Bros. and highest price for any complete-in-box video game. “Complete-in-box” status means the box has been opened and the game inside was used, but the package still retains the cartridge, manual and anything else that would have been included when it was sold at retail. title: $1.5 million Frank Frazetta painting! $15.85 million total at Heritage Auctions Comics and Comic Art
summary: After the bidding battlefield smoke cleared, the winner of Frank Frazetta’s painting The Mucker triumphed with an offer of $1.5 million, leading Heritage’s Comic Art Signature® Auction Nov. 20 and 22 to a total of $10,613,538. Combined with the $5,238,509 achieved by Heritage’s Nov. 19 and 21 Comic Books Signature® Auction, the four-day event shot to a combined total of $15,852,047. The painting served as the cover art for the 1973 Ace paperback reprint of Edgar Rice Burroughs’ novel of the same name and was the crown jewel of a trove of newly available Edgar Rice Burroughs-related material from renowned Burroughs collector, archivist and historian Robert “Bob” Barrett. “Anytime we have a Frazetta painting available, it is exciting,” says Heritage Auctions Vice President Barry Sandoval. “This one really shows Frazetta’s strengths as an artist,

title: Buchmann Galerie brings together late artists Lawrence Carroll and Martin Disler in first joint exhibition
summary: Buchmann Galerie is presenting the exhibition Traces of Memory, which brings together works by Lawrence Carroll and Martin Disler for the first time. Martin Disler and Lawrence Carroll did not know each other personally, yet they shared a life characterised by constant movement and an unceasing commitment to their artistic practice. Both were nomadic figures who repeatedly established their studios in new places, travelled extensively and remained open to new influences and sources of inspiration. Lawrence Carroll lived in Los Angeles until the mid-1980s, before moving to New York, where he remained for several years. After periods in Malibu and a return to Los Angeles, he lived in Venice, Italy from 2007 onwards and, for a time, also maintained a studio in Marquette, Michigan. title: Antonia Kuo connects cosmic phenomena, memory, and new life in solo show at Silverlens
summary: Photographic negatives are recordings of light, time, and atmosphere. They can function like timestamps of an accelerated life where experiences are fleeting and memories are increasingly elusive. For 200 years, photographic capture has been an impulse meant to calm our anxieties about loss and satisfy our desires for retention. Using the same photographic materials and technologies, Antonia Kuo’s photochemical paintings point us to the volatile and unfixed nature of memory and images. Her paintings take us elsewhere far beyond, connecting the microcosm of the body (touch, breath, movement) to the macrocosm of the universe (stars, planets, heavens). A New Sun is an exploration of Kuo’s interdependent worlds—each a feeling, idea, or memory where one relies on the other for the production of dynamic life force. Colors, forms, and patterns

title: Thomas Ruff surveys four decades of analogue and digital experimentation in Los Angeles
summary: David Zwirner is presenting Thomas Ruff: In Series, 1979–2024, the artist’s first major presentation in Los Angeles and his first solo show in the city in over a decade, at the gallery’s 606 N Western Avenue location. One of the most influential photographers working today, Ruff has throughout his career asserted that the photographic method is for him a means to an end: “There’s not one way of making photographs. There are thousands of possibilities you can choose from…. I am just interested in the result and if the result is worth discussing.” This exhibition surveys the artist’s production spanning over four decades, highlighting the multiplicity of procedures he deploys to create his photographs. Providing an overview of Ruff’s most important bodies of work and his in-depth examination of a variety of genres, the photographs

title: Dien Berziga bridges Italian and Chinese visual memories in solo Brussels show
summary: Galerie Nathalie Obadia is presenting Quiet People in Brussels, Dien Berziga's first solo exhibition with the gallery. A graduate of the BA Fine Art at Central Saint Martins, University of the Arts London in 2023, on this occasion, the artist is exhibiting sixteen previously unseen paintings as well as a few sculptures. From the most monumental works to the more intimate formats, all preserve the same sense of intimacy with the viewer. Scale becomes less a measure than a point of entry into the image. A shower of gold seems to fall upon a figure contemplating a landscape ablaze. Coloured grids — like hopscotch squares drawn in chalk — structure the space as much as they disrupt it. Human silhouettes emerge between the hills. But perhaps it is only our eye which, seduced by the sensuous palette, gives itself over to reverie. A joyful melancholy hovers over

title: Luigi Mazzarelli and Ugo La Pietra exhibit at MAN Museo d'arte della Provincia di Nuoro
summary: With exhibitions devoted to Luigi Mazzarelli and Ugo La Pietra, the Museo MAN in Nuoro, Sardinia, continues its programme of exploring and reassessing some of the most radical artistic figures to have emerged in Italy since the 1960s. What connects these diverse artistic trajectories is their development of new research methodologies, pursued with exceptional rigour and remarkable foresight. They address themes that remain highly relevant today, including social transformation, the relationship between the individual, the community and the local environment, and the articulation of a new semantics. Twenty years after the artist’s death, the Museo MAN pays tribute to one of the leading figures in the most radical and complex strands of visual and conceptual art of the second half of the 20th century.

title: Jürgen Klauke examines body, identity, and societal violence in new German show
summary: In November 2026 the Knsthalle Giessen presents a solo exhibition by the German artist Jürgen Klauke. Titled Schlachtfelder, the exhibition brings together photographic series and performance records spanning several decades. At its centre are the interconnections of body, identity, and societal violence. Klauke’s visual worlds offer a view into the tensions between individual self-conception and societal normalization, between visibility and anonymity, vulnerability and the exercise of power. He often refrains from the sensation of the individual image and instead employs serial photography, whose individual exhibits combine to form a monumental overall work. title: Christie's presents Sparkling Fine & Rare Wines & Spirits Sale featuring The Astral Cellar
summary: Christie's Wine & Spirits Department in the Americas is pleased to present its December Fine & Rare Wines & Spirits auction in New York City, a sparkling sale built around the demands of the season: Champagne of exceptional depth and significance alongside a truly consequential fine and rare spirits offering. The online sale—which opens on November 24 and closes on December 8—includes a monumental offering of rare Champagne, including more than 300 bottles and 36 magnums of rare Salon, made solely from the Chardonnay of Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, spanning ten of the house's declared vintages from 1983 to 2013. The depth of the offerings in the sale borders on the archival, with 114 bottles of the 2012, 99 of the 2002, 40 of the 1996, the 1983 by the dozen, the 1999 and 2004 en magnum, and more.
